title: What a shopper's browser gets
grade_reasons: The base is sound: a default store's first load has no zod, no third-party script and no font file, the extras are lazy and gated on the server, and two script budgets exist. But every page sends the store's layout twice, makes one or two server calls that answer nothing and 11 to 47 router requests for pages nobody asked for; eleven working routes share one bundle 98 KB larger than a built page's, and a press on a built page's product tile reloads the whole document. Only first scripts on two store routes are held, with 14 to 16% of room; no check sees a document, a request count or a prefetch, and no measurement saw a themed store, a cart with a product or a checkout with its payment form.

measures.name: First scripts and stylesheet of a first visit, by route
measures.today: Scripts (script tags of the server's HTML, nomodule left out, raw bytes): built page 680,264 (213,261 gzip); product page 777,785; category, tag, search, cart, checkout, account and five more 778,166 each. Of each, 447,102 (133,758 gzip) is React, Next and Turbopack's runtime, the same seven files in all 560 routes. So the app's own share is 233 KB on a built page and 331 KB on the twelve heavier routes. Stylesheet: one render-blocking file for stores, site and admin, 183,124 bytes raw, 25,832 Brotli. Source: digest/storefront-client.md, client-bundles.md and css.md, from the build's chunks.
measures.target_a: Built page at most 615,000 bytes raw (own share 168 KB, about 55 KB gzip). Listing and search at most 650,000. Product page at most 690,000. Cart, checkout and account at most 700,000. A stylesheet of the storefront's own at most 135,000 raw (about 20 KB Brotli).
measures.how_measured: FIRST_SCRIPTS_BUDGETS in e2e/performance.spec.ts, once the budgets item makes it count the server's script tags without the nomodule file (E2E_MEASURE=1 prints each figure). The all-routes check scripts/bundle-budget.mjs that the owner-browser area's BN-11 creates. The stylesheet budget of the styles area's CS-3.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is the framework's 447 KB, which nothing here can remove. The bar lets the app add 38% to it on a built page and 57% on a page that sells or pays. Stated tolerance inside that: the browser's texts in all four languages (24.8 KB, kept by D212 because loading one language made presses get lost), and the forms and carousel a visitor may press before a late script would arrive (13 KB, docs/performance.md:38-51). A B would stop at 640,000 with the stray tables gone and the shared working bundle still on eleven routes.

measures.name: The store document: its size and what is in it twice
measures.today: Home 138,523 bytes raw, 18,691 gzip; 106.7 to 170.3 thousand raw over 12 pages; 66 to 71% is the inline payload. The same 35 rows, 26,151 decoded bytes, are the layout a second time on every page. The listing sends its 9 products twice (24.7 KB). A store in an AI-translated language would add about 93 KB of interface text, of which the browser reads 114 of 1,673 texts. Source: digest/page-payload.md, m/routes.md.
measures.target_a: Nothing twice: under 2,000 bytes of duplicate rows and one html element in the payload. Home under 112,000 bytes raw. /products under 150,000 with each product once. The texts prop of a translated language under 9,000 bytes. Five routes held within 5%.
measures.how_measured: DOCUMENT_BUDGETS in e2e/performance.spec.ts, which the budgets item creates (document bytes and inline payload bytes per route). The duplicate-row count of the review's flight.mjs, moved into the same spec by the layout item. The unit test of uiTextsFor().
measures.why_this_is_a: The payload is the page again as data, which the router needs to hydrate and to move without a reload. That is the floor, about twice the markup here, and the auditors found no oversize prop in it. The tolerance is 2 KB of repeats. The draft's bar of a home document under 60 KB is dropped: no step reaches it, because serving the page static (CA-1) moves the same bytes into the file. A B would leave the listing's second grid.

measures.name: Requests the router makes unasked, for a phone visitor who presses nothing
measures.today: Home: 11 at the top (33 KB), 47 read to the footer (729 KB decoded, 204 KB on the wire), 24 of them for other language, currency and country views. Content page 34, empty cart 42. A multi-country front door 12 (254 KB decoded), none usable. Kaizena Flow's home 8, and 6 admin scripts with them (135 KB on the wire). A full listing of 48 tiles: not measured, about 96 by multiplication. On a local build and in CI, 9 of 11 store pages never go quiet (624 requests in 4 s on search results). Source: digest/prefetch.md, m/routes.md.
measures.target_a: At most 6 on the home, a product page, a content page and the cart, at the top and read to the footer. 0 for another view, for a link that leaves its root layout, and for /admin from the site. At most 20 on a seeded 48-tile listing read to the end. Every page quiet: no router request between 3 and 5 s after load.
measures.how_measured: e2e/prefetch.spec.ts, which the prefetch items create (one table: page, screen, scroll, most router requests). docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/measure-routes.mjs for the full table and storm.mjs for the loop.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is zero: a prefetch earns its request only when the next press opens it. The tolerance is the links a phone shopper most likely presses next, the cart in the bottom bar and one more: about 6 requests and 20 KB. On a listing it is the first screen of tiles. A B would be the draft's 'under 12' with a full listing still fetching every tile it shows.

measures.name: Server calls a view makes for nothing
measures.today: For a visitor with no cart and no wishlist: GET wishlist/saved on 12 of 12 pages (a function call for a 15-byte answer). GET /api/shop/tiles with three queries on the home and /products while both switches are off. POST suggest, with one write, on a search results page nobody typed on. Beside these the document itself is rendered by a function on every view: 148 of 149 prerendered store routes (the caching digest's CA-1). Source: digest/page-payload.md, m/routes.md.
measures.target_a: 0 fetches of the page's own after load on all 12 measured pages for such a visitor. The document served static with no function run: that is the server area's CA-1, and this area's wishlist marker is its first step.
measures.how_measured: The after-load fetch count in e2e/performance.spec.ts (the budgets item adds it at today's 1 and 2; the three fixes lower it to 0). Assertions in e2e/wishlist.spec.ts, e2e/shop-components.spec.ts and e2e/search.spec.ts. For the document, the render-modes script of the server area's CA-16.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is zero and there is no tolerance: each is a function call per view that grows one for one with visits. A store that switches tile stock on, or a visitor who has saved a product, pays for what they use, and that is right.

measures.name: What a press costs
measures.today: A product tile on a built page: a whole document, 42 requests, 104.5 KB on the wire (a link inside the app: 5 requests, 12.9 KB). The cart on a screen of 768 px or more: the drawer is rendered, thrown away, and the page loaded; 3 prefetches and 2 script chunks are fetched for a drawer never shown. The first Add to cart: an answer of 79,467 bytes with the layout twice, then 32 router prefetch events, 20 of them on the network. Source: digest/prefetch.md, page-payload.md.
measures.target_a: Tile press: 0 documents and at most 8 requests. Cart press on a wide screen: 1 document, 0 router requests, 0 prefetches before it. First Add to cart: at most 10 router events, and an answer under 5,000 bytes (the server area's CA-17, after CA-1; until then under 56,000 with the layout sent once).
measures.how_measured: Cases in e2e/prefetch.spec.ts for the tile, the wide cart and the first add (the prefetch items create them). The Add to cart answer's budget in e2e/cart.spec.ts (the budgets item).
measures.why_this_is_a: A press should cost the page it opens and nothing the browser already holds. The floor for a tile press is the product page's own segment and scripts, 5 requests as measured; 8 leaves room for its pictures. A B would keep the full reload on built pages, which are the pages owners build to sell from.

measures.name: The pages real shoppers get, measured
measures.today: Not measured. All 12 store pages in the tables are the bare template: 0 font files, one-row pages, pictures that are drawings of about 1 KB. Each of the six launch themes names two font families. The cart was measured empty, and the checkout load ended on the cart because the demo store takes no payments. Production's demo home document is 203 KB raw against 138 KB locally. Source: m/routes.md, m/prod-pages.md, measure-routes.mjs:27-38.
measures.target_a: A launch-theme store's home, product page and listing, a cart with two lines and the checkout at its payment step are in the measured set, each with budgets within 5%. On the themed home: at most 2 font files and 80 KB of fonts, both preloaded, and the breakpoint sheet once per document. On the checkout: 0 router prefetches while the form shows, and the payment provider's script the only third-party request.
measures.how_measured: The first two gap items create it: a seeded launch-theme store and a payments fixture in CI, added to measure-routes.mjs and to e2e/performance.spec.ts.
measures.why_this_is_a: An A cannot rest on a page no shopper will see. The fonts bar is what kaizenaflow.com reached after trimming: 67 KB for two families (docs/performance.md:97-101). With every finding closed and these pages still unseen, the area is a B.

measures.name: Time on a slow phone
measures.today: Not measured for a store and not held. The review left times out (m/routes.md:8). By idle, 57% of the home page's 834 KB of script had not run; what does run, and for how long, is unknown. Lighthouse runs by hand (pnpm perf); CI holds weight, largest picture and first byte only. docs/performance.md:87 records a largest paint of 3.7 to 4.3 s for kaizenaflow.com on simulated slow 4G on 5 November. Real visitors' figures exist only for stores whose owner switched visit counting on, and never for the cart or checkout.
measures.target_a: Each night, on the launch-theme store's home, product page and listing in production, phone form: Lighthouse performance 90 or more and blocking time at most 200 ms (the median of three runs). In CI: script bytes run by idle held per route within 5%. In the field: Kaizena Flow's own demo stores count visits, and their 75th percentile stays inside the 'good' lines the product shows owners (largest paint 2.5 s, response to a press 200 ms, layout shift 0.1; src/lib/speed.ts:93).
measures.how_measured: The third gap item creates it: a throttled run in measure-routes.mjs, a run-bytes budget in e2e/performance.spec.ts, a nightly workflow beside .github/workflows/live-a11y.yml that runs scripts/perf.mjs --form=mobile --min=90, and commerce.speed_samples for the field figure.
measures.why_this_is_a: Bytes and counts are causes; time is what the shopper feels, and an A needs one figure for it that fails when it slips. 90 is Lighthouse's own line for good and the value scripts/perf.mjs already takes as --min. Tolerance: scores move a few points between runs, so the check takes a median of three and fails on two nights in a row.

measures.name: What holds it
measures.today: First scripts are held on 2 of 56 store routes, with 14 to 16% of room and a polyfill no modern browser loads counted in. Page weight is held on 2 pages with 6 to 10% of room. Nothing holds a document, its payload, a request count, an action's answer or a prefetch. 4 of 947 links state a prefetch policy. Two additions of 10 and 11 November (19 KB on every product page; a server call and 19 KB of lazy script on every product grid) passed every check. Source: e2e/performance.spec.ts:11, 40-50, 126-129; digest/prefetch.md.
measures.target_a: Every store route's first scripts held by the all-routes check, and 8 of them in the browser within 3%. Documents on 5 routes within 5%. Request and prefetch budgets on 6 pages at the measured count plus 2. next/link imported only by three policy wrappers, held by a ratchet that only falls. A budget is lowered in the same change that lowers its measure.
measures.how_measured: e2e/performance.spec.ts, e2e/prefetch.spec.ts, e2e/cart.spec.ts, src/server/ratchet.scan.test.ts (directLinks), src/lib/storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts, and scripts/bundle-budget.mjs from the owner-browser area.
measures.why_this_is_a: This is the grade's second half: each measure above needs a check that fails on the day it slips. The tolerance is the stated room: 3% on scripts, 5% on documents, 2 requests. With more room than that a 19 KB import passes again, as it did on 10 November.
